ext.description: Claude Code conversations that outlive your window: start a task on one device, continue on another, even from your phone. A GUI on top of the Claude Code CLI, with live context, cache and cost figures, and a scratchpad to annotate screenshots and sketch for Claude.
view.cockpit.name: Dashboard
cmd.focusPrompt: Focus the waiting permission prompt or question
cmd.enableUtf8Fix: Fix accents in PowerShell output (install UTF-8 hook)
cfg.tootegaEnabled: Use the local Tootega Code engine. Off (the default), the Cockpit runs on Claude Code only: nothing spawns the local agent and the Engine picker stays hidden. On, the picker comes back and 'Engine' below chooses the default. Requires the TootegaEngine server up (serve.cmd).
cfg.engine: Engine that runs the agent — only applies when 'Tootega enabled' is on. Both speak the same process protocol; what changes is which binary is spawned.
cfg.engine.claude: Claude Code CLI — Anthropic account, subscription limits, plugins, skills and MCP.
cfg.engine.tootega: Tootega Code CLI — local model through the TootegaEngine server. No account, no cost, no data leaving the machine.
cfg.claudePath: Path to the Claude Code CLI executable.
cfg.tootegaPath: Path to the Tootega agent executable (tools/agent.exe of the TootegaEngine build).
cfg.tootegaServer: Address of the TootegaEngine server the agent talks to (host:port). Start it with serve.cmd.
cfg.dateLocale: Locale for dates and times, for example nl-NL or en-GB. Empty: the region of the machine VS Code runs on, or, in a browser, the browser's own locale.
cfg.language: UI language. 'auto' follows the VS Code language; falls back to English.
cfg.permissionMode: Default permission mode passed to the CLI. Reflected (pre-selected) in the Permission dropdown in the panel; change it there to override just the current session.
cfg.allowAgents: Allow the agent to spawn subagents (Task) and workflows (Workflow). Default off — these run extra parallel agents and can burn a lot of tokens, so by default the CLI starts with --disallowedTools Task,Workflow. Turn on to allow them. Reflected in the 'Agents & workflows' checkbox in the panel; toggle there to override just the current session.
cfg.enableTodoTools: Offer the task tools (TodoWrite, TaskCreate/Update/List) on every model. Since CLI 2.1.268 they only exist up to Opus 4.7 / Sonnet 4.6, so on newer models (Opus 5.5…) the Tasks panel stays empty. Turning this on starts the CLI with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1; open tabs pick it up on their next message.
cfg.notifyOnPermission: Show a notification with Allow and Deny when Claude asks for permission and the Cockpit chat is not visible.
cfg.notifyOnComplete: Show a notification when Claude finishes a turn and the Cockpit panel is not visible.
cfg.hideThinking: Hide Claude's thinking blocks in the chat. Off: they are shown, and each one can be collapsed.
cfg.showBashDescription: Show the description Claude gives a Bash command next to its name in the chat.
cfg.spellCheck: Check spelling as you type in the composer, underlining misspelled words. Never auto-corrects — click an underlined word to see suggestions. Off by default.
cfg.expandToolCards: Expand tool call cards by default in the timeline.
cfg.scrollOnSend: Scroll the conversation to the end when you send a message.
cfg.modePins: Model and effort per permission mode: switching to a mode switches to its model and effort, also when Claude leaves plan mode after you approve a plan. Set with the pin in the model popup, or here, for example `{ "plan": { "model": "claude-opus-5-5", "effort": "default" }, "auto": { "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5" } }`.
cfg.userName: Name shown for your messages instead of 'You'. Empty = your OS username.
cfg.ffmpegPath: Path to the ffmpeg executable used for voice dictation capture. Empty = use 'ffmpeg' from PATH.
cfg.voiceLanguage: Language for voice dictation (speech-to-text). Empty = follow the Cockpit UI language.
cfg.voiceCorrect: After stopping dictation, send the text to the internal model for spelling/grammar correction. Clean isolated call (only instruction + text; no tools/MCP/context).
cfg.debugLog: Write detailed diagnostic logs to the "Cockpit for Claude Code" output channel (cache keep-alive, stats persistence, cache reset/compaction, session lifecycle). Off by default to avoid noise.
cfg.systemPromptQuiet: Directive injected at the very start of the system prompt, on every CLI start: the agent stops narrating the execution and stops closing with a report or summary. Independent of the switch below — leave the box empty to inject nothing.
cfg.systemPromptEnabled: Inject the text below into the system prompt every time the CLI starts (including a respawn that continues the same conversation). Off by default.
cfg.systemPromptText: Text appended to the system prompt. Supports placeholders resolved against this machine: ${defaultShell}, ${psVersion}, ${winPathStyle}, ${projectPathWin}, ${projectPathGitBash}, ${projectPathWsl}, ${wslRow}, ${os}, ${tempDir}. A line whose placeholder refers to something absent here (no WSL, no Git Bash) is dropped whole, so the agent is never told about a shell it does not have; an unknown ${name} is left untouched.
cfg.otelEnabled: Start a local OpenTelemetry receiver (127.0.0.1) and turn on the Claude CLI telemetry export so the Usage panel can show lines of code, sessions, commits and edit-tool decisions per model. Opt-in, off by default. Loopback traffic only; never logs credentials or response text.
cfg.internalModel: Model used for Cockpit's internal AI calls (dictation correction, slash-command help). These are clean, isolated calls (no tools/MCP/context). Haiku is fastest/cheapest.
cfg.verbosity: How much of the timeline to show (display only — does not change the agent). Verbose = everything; Necessary = edits + final explanations; Dialogo = edits + what it's doing; Quiet = final explanations only.
cfg.model: Default model for new sessions. Leave 'default' to let the CLI choose. There is no fixed list here: the Model dropdown in the panel offers what your account actually has (live discovery); change it there to override just the current session.
cfg.effort: Default reasoning effort for new sessions. 'CLI default' uses your ~/.claude/settings.json effortLevel. Reflected (pre-selected) in the Effort dropdown in the panel; change it there to override just the current session.
cfg.uploadRetentionDays: Files you dropped or pasted into the chat are kept in .cockpit/uploads/ of the workspace. Files older than this many days are deleted when Cockpit starts. 0 keeps them all.
cfg.autoResumeLastSession: When opening a folder, automatically resume the most recent session for that folder (loads its history). Turn off to always start empty.
cfg.autosave: Auto-save an open file before Claude reads or writes it, so the agent works on the latest content.
cmd.daemonInstall: Install daemon (keep Claude running across windows)
cmd.daemonStopSession: Stop this session's process in the daemon
cfg.daemonIdleStopHours: Stop a daemon-owned Claude process after this many hours idle with no window attached and no prompt waiting (it resumes on the next message). 0 = never. Applied when the daemon is (re)installed.
cfg.thinking: Extended thinking for the Claude processes Cockpit starts.
cfg.thinking.off: Force thinking off (MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 and alwaysThinkingEnabled=false), as earlier Cockpit versions always did.
cmd.openInSidebar: Move to the side bar chat
cfg.preferredLocation: Where new conversations open: the side bar chat (like the official extension) or an editor tab. A conversation is in one place at a time; "Open in editor" and "Move to the side bar chat" move it.
cfg.autoCompact: Default auto-compact for new conversations: "auto" (the CLI's own window), "off", or the window in tokens (100000 to 1000000) at which older messages are summarised. Each conversation can override it from the settings menu in its prompt box.
